cands.name: Frances Jackson
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 45 (southwestern Cumberland County) since 2023. Former middle school teacher, adjunct political science professor, and community and transit planner for the Cumberland County Metropolitan Planning Organization. Holds a Ph.D. in public policy and administration. Ran unsuccessfully for the seat in 2020.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended in the 2026 cycle by Fair Map Fight Club (a Sway voting group run by Tara Arbitter).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Frances Jackson was born or when, or whether she ever lived outside North Carolina. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year, and the pages we reviewed show no statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B workers, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. Her campaign site says she sponsored a bill to cut property and vehicle taxes for disabled veterans and a bill to restore teacher retiree health coverage, but we found no independent record of the bills, so we left them out. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or public stances on data centers or development.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she grew up in Fayetteville and is a third-generation graduate of E.E. Smith Senior High School, but no source gives her birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2023. Before that she worked as a community and transit planner for the Cumberland County Metropolitan Planning Organization (her campaign site says 27 years in local government), taught middle school, and was an adjunct political science professor. Her campaign site also says she served as a magistrate. She holds a Ph.D. in public policy and administration.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service (a current member of the House since 2023) and a long public policy and planning career with an advanced policy degree, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget.
